certificate.title: AI-Supported Analysis, Review & Validation

course.description: Learn a repeatable, evidence-grounded way to use AI to extract facts, test work, analyze financial information, reconcile records, identify exceptions, validate calculations, and reach supported finance conclusions.
intendedAudience: Finance professionals beginning AI-supported review and decision-support work
learningOutcomes: Frame a finance review so AI receives the right objective, evidence, criteria, and output requirements.
Extract decision-relevant facts while preserving source traceability.
Evaluate evidence against stated rules and criteria.
Analyze financial data and distinguish supported explanations from speculation.
Detect anomalies and prioritize exceptions without treating unusual items as errors.
Validate calculations, models, and reports using independent checks.
Apply materiality, uncertainty, and professional judgment to reach a supported conclusion.

modules.description: Turn contracts and supporting documents into a traceable fact set without inventing missing terms.

lessons.content:
Document extraction is more than summarization. The goal is to locate facts that matter to a defined finance question, preserve where each fact came from, normalize the result, and expose gaps or conflicts. Before using AI, define the target fields and the decision they support. Require page, section, or clause references. Tell AI to label absent information as missing instead of guessing.

Inspect the output for quiet failure modes: skipped amendments, definitions interpreted out of context, dates confused with execution dates, monetary terms detached from conditions, and narrative paraphrases that change the original meaning. Verify the most decision-relevant fields directly against the source.

tasks.instructions:
**Situation:** Finney Incorporated is preparing its quarter-end vendor accrual review. A services agreement contains the commercial terms needed to determine the period, fee structure, invoicing terms, and termination rights.

**Task:** Extract the specified contract facts into the provided template and identify any fields the agreement does not support.

**Action:**

1. Download and review the supplied source files and output template. Identify the decision, required fields, and authoritative evidence before using AI.

3. Cross-check the AI-assisted work against the source files. Reperform material calculations, verify citations and classifications, and correct or flag anything unsupported.
4. Complete the supplied output template, confirm that every required item is addressed, and save the final deliverable for submission.

**Expected Result:** Submit a completed fact sheet with source references, a missing-information list, and a short verification note.

modules.description: Compare transactions and support against explicit policy criteria and distinguish facts from judgment.

lessons.content:
Criteria-based review requires two inputs: the evidence and the rule set. Ask AI to translate the rule set into a testable checklist before applying it. This exposes vague requirements and prevents the model from silently inventing policy. Each conclusion should identify the criterion, relevant evidence, result, and any uncertainty.

Do not reduce the output to pass or fail when the evidence supports more useful categories. “Pass,” “exception,” “insufficient evidence,” and “requires judgment” make the next action visible. Verify every material exception and every result that depends on an interpretation rather than a direct rule.

modules.description: Quantify period-over-period movement and produce evidence-supported explanations rather than plausible stories.

lessons.content:
Variance analysis has two distinct stages: calculate what changed and investigate why. AI may help with both, but the first stage must remain reproducible and the second must remain evidence-bound. Define comparison periods, sign conventions, materiality thresholds, dimensional cuts, and the source hierarchy before analysis.

An explanation should connect a quantified movement to supporting records. “Higher marketing spend” restates the variance; “three campaign invoices totaling $84,000 drove 72% of the increase” explains it. Label unverified explanations as hypotheses and name the evidence needed to confirm them.

modules.description: Match records across systems, explain legitimate differences, and isolate unresolved breaks.

lessons.content:
A reconciliation is a completeness and agreement test between independently maintained records. Begin by defining populations, keys, tolerances, timing rules, and the treatment of duplicates. AI can propose matches and group exceptions, but every match should remain explainable and every transformation reproducible.

Use categories that preserve meaning: exact match, acceptable tolerance, timing difference, supported reconciling item, unmatched, and duplicate. Never let a high similarity score substitute for evidence. Confirm that the reconciled totals bridge from source to source and that no records disappeared during preprocessing.

modules.description: Use patterns and criteria to prioritize unusual items without assuming unusual means wrong.

lessons.content:
Anomaly detection narrows attention; it does not prove error or fraud. Define the risk question and relevant indicators before asking AI to flag items. Useful signals may include duplicates, unusual timing, round-dollar amounts, rare accounts, threshold clustering, unexpected users, new vendors, or combinations of factors.

Require AI to state why each item was flagged and what additional evidence would confirm or dismiss the concern. Evaluate both precision and coverage: too many weak flags waste reviewer time, while an overly narrow test misses meaningful exceptions. Rank findings by potential impact, strength of signal, and urgency.

modules.description: Test model logic and report integrity using independent recomputation, structural checks, and tie-outs.

lessons.content:
Validation asks whether a calculation or report is complete, internally consistent, reproducible, and fit for its intended decision. Do not ask AI only to “check the file.” Specify the assertions: formulas are consistent, inputs are complete, totals tie, signs and units are correct, assumptions are disclosed, and outputs agree to authoritative sources.

Use independent recalculation for high-risk outputs. Inspect formulas and dependencies, not just displayed values. Look for hard-coded overrides, broken ranges, hidden omissions, inconsistent periods, circular logic, stale inputs, and rounding differences. A validation report should separate confirmed defects from design choices and unresolved questions.

modules.description: Convert mixed review evidence into an accountable decision with explicit uncertainty, materiality, and escalation.

lessons.content:
The final finance task is rarely just finding an issue. It is deciding what the evidence means and what should happen next. AI can organize facts, compare options, and expose assumptions, but professional judgment determines materiality, sufficiency, acceptable risk, and escalation.

A supported conclusion distinguishes known facts, reasonable inferences, unresolved uncertainty, and the applicable decision threshold. It should state the disposition—accept, adjust, investigate, or escalate—and why. Ask what evidence would change the conclusion. Avoid false precision and make the accountable human reviewer visible.

pages.content:
AI can accelerate finance review, but fluent output is not evidence. A dependable review begins with a bounded question, an identified evidence set, explicit evaluation criteria, and a required output format. The human remains accountable for materiality, ambiguity, professional judgment, and the final conclusion.

Treat the AI response as a workpaper draft. Every important claim should be traceable to an input, reproducible calculation, or stated inference. Separate facts from interpretations. Make missing evidence visible. A strong prompt does more than ask for an answer: it defines the task, supplies the authoritative materials, tells AI how to handle uncertainty, and requires citations or record-level references.

The seven-step method is deliberately repetitive. The finance scenario changes, but the control structure remains stable: orient, ground, direct, inspect, verify, judge, and conclude.

scenes.body: AI can organize evidence and expose patterns quickly. The source records and accountable finance professional still determine what is true.
scenes.title: AI is a reviewer, not the authority

pages.title: The evidence-grounded review method

pages.content:
Across all 21 exercises, the subject matter changed but the control pattern did not. Reliable AI-supported finance work begins with a bounded question and authoritative evidence. It uses explicit criteria, inspectable calculations, and traceable findings. It ends with a human-owned judgment that states what is known, what remains uncertain, and what happens next.

The practical standard is not whether AI produced an answer. It is whether another qualified reviewer can follow the work from question to evidence, from evidence to analysis, and from analysis to conclusion. Use the seven-step method whenever AI helps review a contract, policy, variance, reconciliation, exception population, model, or close decision.
